title.narrative: Supporting the School Education Sector Plan

description.narrative: The results-based lending (RBL)program will assist the Government of Nepal in reforming the school education system through the implementation of its School Education Sector Plan (SESP) in a sector-wide approach (SWAp) supported by eight development partners, including the Asian Development Bank (ADB). The RBL program will strengthen equity, quality, and resilience of school education by helping the government (i) enhance learning provisions for basic and secondary schools; (ii) strengthen teaching and learning in basic and secondary schools; (iii) accelerate the recovery from learning losses caused by the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic; and (iv) improve the capacity of governments, especially local governments, for education planning, monitoring, and reporting.

description.narrative: Equity, quality and resilience of the school education strengthened.

Grade 3 students achieving minimum proficiency in reading and numeracy increased by 3 percentage points (disaggregation by sex, background, and disability)b (Baseline to be established by 2025) (DLI2) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not yet due. Data Source: Education Review Office: NARN report

Share of students with disabilities in basic education enrollment increased to 1.00% (boys: 1.12%, girls: 0.98%), (disaggregation by background). (DLI 1 ii) Achievement: 0.42 Progress/Status: Share of students with disabilities in basic education enrollment has reached 0.42% (boys: 0.45%, girls: 0.38%), which is lower than the baseline. Data still being gathered for this year. Data Source: EMIS annual consolidated status report

No. of students enrolled in science in grades 11-12 as a share of total enrollment increased—boys to 20.0%, girls to 14.0% (disaggregation by ethnic and economic background [Dalits and other DAGs] and disability) (DLI-1) (OP 1.1.1 and OP 2.2.1) Achievement: 21.4 Progress/Status: Students enrolled in science subjects in Grade 11 and 12 in total enrollment reached 21.54% for boys and 21.44% for girls, with a total GER of 21.4 % (2025 Flash 1 report). Data Source: EMIS/National Examinations Board: annual consolidated status report

Survival to grade 10 increased to 75.00% (boys: 74.59%, girls: 75.37%) (disaggregation by background and disability)b (FY2022 baseline: 66.14%, male: 65.77%, female: 66.51%) Achievement: 69.9 Progress/Status: Survival to grade 10 has reached 69.9% (boys: 69.9%, girls: 69.8%). Further disaggregation by background and disability not available. Data Source: EMIS annual consolidated status report
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Learning provisions for basic and secondary schools enhanced. Indicator: Revised pro-poor scholarship scheme for equal opportunity among students implemented nationwide in grades 6-12 (DLI4) Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: The pro-poor scholarship guideline has been revised and is being implemented from FY2024-25. BRM 2026 will discuss the actual status on it. Data Source: EMIS annual consolidated status report

Output: Learning recovery accelerated. Indicator: 150 local governments implementing activities as per the recovery and accelerated learning plan in at least 80% schools by 2024 (2022 baseline: not applicable) (DLI 8) Achievement: 150 Progress/Status: Achieved. All selected 150 local governments have already developed their action plan and have been implementing the ReAL plan in line with the Standard Operating Procedure. Data Source: EMIS annual consolidated status report

Output: Teaching and learning in basic and secondary schools strengthened. Indicator: At least 80% of local governments conducting basic level examination for grade 8 by using the standardized test items (DLI 7) Achievement: 21 Progress/Status: The process of accessing an item bank of standardized test items for Basic Level Examinations is being discussed by NEB with its technical team. An additional standardized test for Basic Level Examinations (Grade 8) based on the revised framework and curriculum is in the development process. The pilot testing of the Items was done i March 2024. Achieved for Year 2, NEB data shows that 21 % of Local Government used the standardized test items for the 24/25 BLE. Data Source: MOEST annual status reports

Output: Learning provisions for basic and secondary schools enhanced. Indicator: Number of teachers demonstrating improved knowledge of disability-inclusive education increased to 500 (disaggregation by sex, background, and disability) Progress/Status: The government is trying to improve knowledge of disability-inclusive education among teachers, but needs close collaboration with local governments going forward. Data Source: EMIS annual consolidated status report Actual value:

Output: Teaching and learning in basic and secondary schools strengthened. Indicator: Secondary schools with full complement of math, science, and English subject teachers in grades 9-10 increased to 38% (DLI 5 ii) (disaggregation by sex and background) Achievement: 31.3% Progress/Status: IVA confirms that the proportion of basic schools that have full complement of math, science and English subject teachers in grades 6-8 in total number of basic schools increased to at least 37.0% and proportion of secondary schools that have full complement of Math, Science and English subject teachers in grades 9-10 is increased at least to 34.0%) has been verified and concluded that the achievement has exceeded the DLI targets for Year 4. Thus, this DLI has been fully achieved.
